title: Transitivity and summand preservation of rational purity
statement:
The purity isomorphisms of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] are transitive in coefficient
extensions, and preserve idempotent summands (via
[thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] and the descent
functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]).

proof.text: Work with the purity isomorphisms of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], in its stated setting: $f:X\to Y$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between separated finite-type schemes over the fixed algebraic closure $k$ of a finite field of characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$. Both schemes are noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has just the ideals $0,k$), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. The integral category underlying [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] agrees, with the same completed coefficient sheaf and reductions, with the derived-complete category by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Every such lattice has a uniform finite-level Tor interval by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], so the hypotheses of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] hold for all these lattices. Use its simultaneous integral family $\gamma^I_E:H^I_E\Rightarrow G^I_E$, with $H^I_E=Lf_E^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and $G^I_E=Rf_E^!$, and its exact linear comparison maps $a^I_{F/E},b^I_{F/E}$. The rational maps under discussion are the rationalizations of this compatible integral construction, as in [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]; we do not choose independent lifts separately for individual objects or coefficient fields.

source.place: Proof, lattice clause: verify the actual coefficient categories and select a compatible integral family before localizing

proof.text:
Let $Q_E$ denote scalar localization at $\varpi_E$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the supplied exact linear functors $H^I_E,G^I_E$ and the natural transformation $\gamma^I_E$ from Step 1. Write their extensions as $H_E,G_E$ and $\gamma_{E,K}=Q_E(\gamma^I_{E,K})$. The inverse is $Q_E((\gamma^I_{E,K})^{-1})$, since functors preserve the two inverse equations. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], every rational morphism can be written $u/\varpi_E^r$ with $u$ integral. Multiply the integral naturality equation $G^I_E(u)\gamma^I_{E,K}=\gamma^I_{E,L}H^I_E(u)$ by $\varpi_E^{-r}$ to obtain
$$G_E(u/\varpi_E^r)\gamma_{E,K}=\gamma_{E,L}H_E(u/\varpi_E^r).$$
For an isomorphism $v:K\to L$ between two lattice presentations this is $\gamma_{E,L}=G_E(v)\gamma_{E,K}H_E(v)^{-1}$. This is independence under change of presentation, not multiplication of the purity map by an unspecified unit. In particular rational idempotents, even ones not represented by integral idempotents, satisfy the same naturality equation.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: replace the informal denominator/unit assertion by localized naturality

proof.text:
For $E\subset F$ use $T^W_{F/E}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], whose integral functor is ordinary derived tensor by the completed coefficient sheaf, exactly the presentation of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $u=\varpi_F$. The image of $t$ in $F=S[1/u]$ is nonzero and hence invertible, including for ramified extensions. It localizes the exact comparisons $a^I,b^I$ and their purity square, unit, composition and shift equations to natural isomorphisms
$$a_{F/E}:T^X_{F/E}H_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_FT^Y_{F/E},\qquad b_{F/E}:T^X_{F/E}G_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_FT^Y_{F/E}$$
satisfying
$$b_{F/E,K}T^X_{F/E}(\gamma_{E,K})=\gamma_{F,T^Y_{F/E}K}a_{F/E,K}.$$

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: apply semilinear scalar localization to the integral purity square and all comparison equations

proof.text:
To display transitivity, abbreviate $T_{L/F}$ by $T_2$, $T_{F/E}$ by $T_1$, and let $A^W:T^W_2T^W_1\to T^W_{L/E}$ be the tensor associator for $E\subset F\subset L$. The composite $b$ comparison is $B=b_{L/F,T^Y_1K}T^X_2(b_{F/E,K})$, and the composite $a$ comparison is $D=a_{L/F,T^Y_1K}T^X_2(a_{F/E,K})$. Apply $T^X_2$ to the Step 3 square for $F/E$ at $K$, then use the Step 3 square for $L/F$ at $T^Y_1K$:
$$B\,T^X_2T^X_1(\gamma_{E,K})=b_{L/F,T^Y_1K}T^X_2(\gamma_{F,T^Y_1K})T^X_2(a_{F/E,K})=\gamma_{L,T^Y_2T^Y_1K}\,D.$$
The comparison composition laws from [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], localized in Step 3, say $b_{L/E,K}A^X_{G_EK}=G_L(A^Y_K)B$ and $a_{L/E,K}A^X_{H_EK}=H_L(A^Y_K)D$. Using naturality of $A^X$ at $\gamma_{E,K}$, then these laws, then naturality of $\gamma_L$ at $A^Y_K$:
$$b_{L/E,K}T^X_{L/E}(\gamma_{E,K})A^X_{H_EK}=G_L(A^Y_K)B\,T^X_2T^X_1(\gamma_{E,K})=G_L(A^Y_K)\gamma_{L,T^Y_2T^Y_1K}D=\gamma_{L,T^Y_{L/E}K}a_{L/E,K}A^X_{H_EK}.$$
Cancel the isomorphism $A^X_{H_EK}$. This is exactly the direct $E\subset L$ coefficient square. For the identity extension both comparisons are identities. Hence successive extension and direct extension agree, with the specified associators.

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: paste the two squares by interchange and substitute the localized associator equations

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to $H_E,G_E$ with the exact scalar comparisons of Steps 3–4. Their unit, associator and shift hypotheses were verified there. The purity components satisfy its natural-transformation compatibility, and so do their inverses, since the coefficient square rearranges to
$$T^X_{F/E}(\gamma_{E,K}^{-1})b_{F/E,K}^{-1}=a_{F/E,K}^{-1}\gamma_{F,T^Y_{F/E}K}^{-1}.$$
For completeness, an object of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is $(E,K)$ and a morphism from $(E,K)$ to $(F,L)$ is represented over a common finite field $M$ by $u:T^Y_{M/E}K\to T^Y_{M/F}L$. Put $U=T^Y_{M/E}K$, $V=T^Y_{M/F}L$, and abbreviate the comparison components at $K,L$ by $a_E,a_F,b_E,b_F$. The two descended functor images are represented by $a_F^{-1}H_M(u)a_E$ and $b_F^{-1}G_M(u)b_E$, by the cited descent statement. Their naturality square is the explicit equality
$$\begin{aligned}
(b_F^{-1}G_M(u)b_E)T^X_{M/E}(\gamma_{E,K})
&=b_F^{-1}G_M(u)\gamma_{M,U}a_E\\
&=b_F^{-1}\gamma_{M,V}H_M(u)a_E\\
&=T^X_{M/F}(\gamma_{F,L})(a_F^{-1}H_M(u)a_E).
\end{aligned}$$
The first and last equalities are Step 3, the middle is Step 2. The cited descent statement asserts that compatible transformations and their equations descend: this includes invariance under enlargement of $M$ and under equality of common-stage representatives, whose associator equations are those checked in Step 4. The descended inverse equations are represented by the finite-stage inverse equations. This proves presentation independence and an invertible natural purity transformation at the algebraically closed coefficient stage.

source.place: Proof, independence from finite stage and presentation: use the actual common-stage descent formula

proof.text:
At either field stage, write $H,G,\gamma$ for the two functors and the natural isomorphism of Steps 2 and 5. For an idempotent $e:K\to K$, naturality gives $G(e)\gamma_K=\gamma_KH(e)$, and multiplying by $\gamma_K^{-1}$ gives $H(e)\gamma_K^{-1}=\gamma_K^{-1}G(e)$. In the Karoubi envelope of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] set
$$c_e=G(e)\gamma_KH(e),\qquad d_e=H(e)\gamma_K^{-1}G(e).$$
These are morphisms $(HK,H(e))\to(GK,G(e))$ and back, since multiplying either by its source and target idempotents does not change it. The two naturality equations and $e^2=e$ give
$$d_ec_e=H(e)\gamma_K^{-1}G(e)\gamma_KH(e)=H(e),\qquad c_ed_e=G(e)\gamma_KH(e)\gamma_K^{-1}G(e)=G(e).$$
These are exactly the two identity morphisms in that envelope. Thus purity restricts to the idempotent summand. The summands are actual objects of the coefficient categories: [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian] supplies a splitting in the raw finite-field rational category, with the noetherian, finite-dimensional, invertibility hypotheses verified in Step 1; [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] supplies idempotent completeness and the exact equivalence with the envelope for the algebraically closed category. No Karoubi completion is silently inserted in either coefficient-category definition.

source.place: Proof, idempotent-completeness clause: write the restricted map and both inverse equations

proof.text:
To identify the restriction with purity on an actual summand, let $i:J\to K$, $r:K\to J$ satisfy $ri=1_J$, $ir=e$. Then $G(r)\gamma_KH(i)=\gamma_JH(ri)=\gamma_J$, by naturality; its inverse is $H(r)\gamma_K^{-1}G(i)$. For another splitting $i':J'\to K$, $r':K\to J'$, the maps $r'i:J\to J'$ and $ri':J'\to J$ are inverse, since $ei=i$, $ei'=i'$, and naturality for $r'i$ identifies the two restricted purity maps. Finally each coefficient-extension functor of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] carries $ri=1$ and $ir=e$ to the corresponding splitting equations. Write $T_X=T^X_{F/E}$, $T_Y=T^Y_{F/E}$, and $s_E=G_E(r)\gamma_{E,K}H_E(i)=\gamma_{E,J}$. Multiply the coefficient square at $K$ on the left by $G_F(T_Yr)$ and on the right by $T_X(H_Ei)$. Naturality of $b$ at $r$ and of $a$ at $i$ rewrites its two sides as
$$b_{F/E,J}T_X(s_E)=G_F(T_Yr)\gamma_{F,T_YK}H_F(T_Yi)a_{F/E,J}=\gamma_{F,T_YJ}a_{F/E,J}.$$
The last equality uses $T_Y(r)T_Y(i)=1$ and naturality of $\gamma_F$ at $T_Yi$. Thus the restricted map satisfies exactly the coefficient square at $J$; Step 4's associator equations identify its successive and direct extensions. For common-stage descent, let $\overline H,\overline G,\overline\gamma$ be the functors and transformation of Step 5. The classes of any splitting maps satisfy $[r][i]=1$ and $[i][r]=[e]$, because composition is computed at a common finite stage. Naturality from Step 5 gives
$$\overline G([r])\overline\gamma_K\overline H([i])=\overline\gamma_J\overline H([r][i])=\overline\gamma_J,$$
with inverse $\overline H([r])\overline\gamma_K^{-1}\overline G([i])$. If the splitting is only specified in the common-stage category, its existence is Step 6; the same displayed calculation uses its actual morphism classes. Step 5's representative independence makes this restriction independent of the chosen common stage. Therefore taking the summand commutes with finite extension, successive extension and common-stage descent, independently of a chosen splitting.
